sites.name: Indian Mounds Park
sites.description: This bluff-top park preserves Woodland period burial mounds overlooking the Mississippi River.
sites.notes: Outdoor archaeological park with no staffed visitor facility.

sites.name: Quincy Museum
sites.description: Exhibits include Native American artifacts from western Illinois.

sites.name: Old Lincoln Courtroom & Museum
sites.description: This restored courtroom includes exhibits on local history and Abraham Lincoln’s legal career.

sites.name: New Philadelphia Town Site
sites.description: Archaeological investigations have documented the layout and lifeways of New Philadelphia, the first town in the United States founded and platted by an African American.
sites.notes: Open archaeological landscape with no central visitor facility.

sites.name: Ray Norbut State Fish & Wildlife Area
sites.description: This large state area includes land along the Illinois River that has been the focus of archaeological research on Native American use of riverine environments.
sites.notes: Primarily a natural resource area with limited interpretive infrastructure.

sites.name: Pike County Historical Society Museum
sites.description: Collections include artifacts from Native American occupations and early Euro-American settlement in Pike County.
sites.notes: Limited online presence; verify details locally.

sites.name: Center for American Archeology Museum and Visitor Center
sites.description: Exhibits interpret the archaeology of the Illinois River valley and ongoing archaeological investigations.

sites.name: Two Rivers National Wildlife Refuge
sites.description: The refuge protects floodplain habitats at the confluence of the Illinois and Mississippi rivers, an area long used by Native American groups.

sites.name: Principia School of Nations Museum
sites.description: The museum contains collections of American Indian cultural materials used for educational purposes within the school curriculum.

sites.name: Village of Elsah Museum
sites.description: The museum preserves the history of Elsah and surrounding communities.
